- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward by 3–8% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion rule: subtract 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.5 → +0.3), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
